clips.label: Question 1
clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Five-step needs analysis sequence. What is the primary objective of conducting a formal needs analysis before selecting audiovisual equipment? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Lock in final hardware model numbers and wholesale dealer pricing prior to stakeholder interviews. Option B. Generate detailed point-to-point conduit schedules and rack elevation drawings for architectural bidding. Option C. Complete post-integration performance verification test checklists defined by ANSI/AVIXA 10:2013 standards. Option D. Identify the activities end users must perform and define the functional descriptions of systems supporting those activities.

clips.label: Question 1, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Lock in final hardware model numbers and wholesale dealer pricing prior to stakeholder interviews. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "Lock in final hardware model numbers and…interviews" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. Decisive rule: A needs analysis identifies the activities end users must perform with the AV system and develops nontechnical functional descriptions before any equipment is selected. Best answer: Identify the activities end users must perform and define the functional descriptions of systems supporting those activities.

clips.label: Question 3
clips.text: Exam area A. Topic: Open-ended stakeholder interview questions. Closed-ended questions confirming specific hardware delivery dates and budget caps. Option B. Open-ended questions such as asking what they would like to see done differently or better. Option C. Directive questions steering participants toward preferred vendor displays and switchers. Option D. Leading questions assuming the existing legacy system topology must be duplicated.

clips.label: Question 73, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. 9 kg (20 lb). Incorrect. Not this one: "9 kg (20 lb)" uses the wrong value, unit, or relationship for the stated quantities. Decisive rule: Safe Working Load (SWL) equals the component's ultimate load limit divided by a safety factor of 5; therefore a 45 kg total suspended load requires every link in the mounting chain to be rated for at least 5 × 45 = 225 kg. Best answer: 225 kg (495 lb).

clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Three-phase phase-to-neutral vs phase-to-phase voltage relation. In a commercial facility supplied by a three-phase wye electrical service, how does phase-to-neutral voltage relate to phase-to-phase voltage? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Phase-to-neutral voltage equals phase-to-phase voltage multiplied by a 3.41 factor. Option D. Three-phase wye systems lack neutral conductors and supply 480-volt direct current.

clips.label: Question 90
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: MEP branch-circuit and heat-load coordination sequence. Arrange the steps for specifying AV electrical branch circuits and HVAC thermal loads for the MEP engineering team in the proper sequence. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Gather rated voltage, current, power consumption, and efficiency data for every AV device under typical simultaneous use. Step 2: Group receptacles onto dedicated single-phase AV branch circuits so each circuit stays at or below its continuous current limit (e.g., 16 A on a 20 A circuit). Step 3: Calculate total room and rack heat dissipation in kJ/hr or Btu/hr, adjusting power amplifiers for actual efficiency and duty cycle. Step 4: Document circuit locations, grounding notes, harmonic neutral demands, and thermal loads on the A&E coordination drawings for the MEP engineers.

segments.text: A legacy display controller accepts IP control commands via unencrypted Telnet. How should network security mitigate clear-text credentials?

segments.label: Response instruction
segments.text: Choose one labeled answer area.

segments.label: Option A
segments.text: Option A. Route control traffic across the public DMZ subnet using default administrator port assignments.

segments.label: Option B
segments.text: Option B. Enable port mirroring on the core switch to log unencrypted terminal sessions to a local drive.

segments.label: Option C
segments.text: Option C. Isolate the device on a dedicated AV VLAN and restrict access with router access control lists.

segments.label: Option D
segments.text: Option D. Configure dynamic host configuration protocols to generate randomized session credentials hourly.

clips.label: Question 102, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Route control traffic across the public DMZ subnet using default administrator port assignments. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "Route control traffic across the public DMZ…port assignments" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. Decisive rule: When a device relies on an insecure clear-text protocol like Telnet, isolating the device and its controller on a dedicated AV VLAN and blocking Telnet at the router via an ACL mitigates the snooping risk. Best answer: Isolate the device on a dedicated AV VLAN and restrict access with router access control lists.

High-Throughput Data class designed for background file transfers and bulk replication. Option D. Broadcast Video class designed for real-time unbuffered and non-elastic media feeds.

clips.label: Question 105
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Networked AV security risk assessment and mitigation workflow. Order the steps an AV designer follows when coordinating networked AV security and risk mitigation with the client's IT security stakeholders. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Identify the client's mission, CIA triad priorities, security posture, and operational, network, and physical stakeholders. Step 2: Catalog system vulnerabilities and threats in a prioritized Risk Register rated by probability and severity impact. Plenum insulation reduces high-frequency capacitive attenuation over extended runs. Option D. Plenum construction provides structural tensile strength for unsupported cable spans.

clips.label: Question 129
clips.text: Exam area B. Topic: Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) and life-safety compliance sequence. Put the steps for ensuring life-safety, fire-code, and regulatory compliance across an AV design in the proper professional order. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Identify the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) and gather all applicable national, regional, and local building, electrical, fire, and accessibility codes. Step 2: Compare overlapping codes and standards and adopt the most stringent requirement wherever interpretations conflict. Step 3: Integrate life-safety interfaces (fire alarm mute/override, plenum ratings, sprinkler clearances, ADA reach/protrusion limits) into the AV design drawings and specifications. Step 4: Verify and document life-safety and regulatory compliance with the AHJ and allied professionals before final sign-off.

Duration calculates equipment lead times, while effort tracks electrical subcontractor progress. Option C. Duration reflects elapsed calendar time, while effort measures active labor hours. Option D. Duration determines code-mandated work windows, while effort serves internal job cost accounting.

clips.label: Interaction rationale 135
clips.text: Work from the governing relationship or dependency, not from memory alone. Critical frequency Fc = (3 × v) ÷ RSD = (3 × 1125 ft/s) ÷ 15 ft = 3375 ÷ 15 = 225 Hz. Below ~225 Hz, room modes dominate the acoustic response. CTS-D cue: follow the signal flow and keep acoustic, electrical, and level concepts distinct.

clips.label: Question 146
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Conceptual projection and display design sequence. Order the steps for developing a conceptual projection display design from content classification through projector lens positioning. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Classify the primary viewing category (Passive, BDM, ADM, or Full-Motion Video) based on the detail viewers must resolve. Step 2: Apply DISCAS and a 30-degree sightline study to determine required image height, viewing cone, and nearest/farthest viewer distances. Step 3: Calculate required projector lumens from ambient light at the screen, ISCR minimum contrast ratio, screen area, screen gain, and the 0.75 derating factor. Step 4: Select the projector and lens throw ratio to establish the throw distance and horizontal/vertical offsets.

clips.label: Question 152, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Microphones must maintain three times the distance to ceiling loudspeakers as to the talker. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "Microphones must maintain three times the…as to the talker" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. Best answer: Adjacent microphone spacing must be three times the talker-to-microphone distance.

clips.label: Question 154
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Direct-connected loudspeaker amplifier sizing workflow. Order the four steps for specifying the required power amplifier output for a directly connected (low-impedance) loudspeaker system. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Determine the target average Sound Pressure Level (Lp) required at the farthest listener distance (D2). Step 2: Add the appropriate program headroom allowance (H = 10 dB for speech or 20 dB for music). Step 3: Calculate the Electrical Power Required (EPR) using the loudspeaker's 1 W / 1 m sensitivity (Ls) and inverse-square distance loss 20 × log(D2 ÷ Dr). Step 4: Round the calculated wattage up to a commercially available power amplifier rating at the circuit's nominal impedance.

clips.label: Question 171
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: PAG and NAG acoustic stability verification workflow. Sequence the steps for performing the mathematical acoustic stability test (confirming NAG < PAG) on a speech reinforcement design. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Measure or extract from drawings the key distances: talker to farthest listener (D0), mic to nearest speaker (D1), farthest listener to nearest speaker (D2), talker to mic (Ds), and Equivalent Acoustic Distance (EAD). Step 2: Calculate Needed Acoustic Gain: NAG = 20 × log10(D0 ÷ EAD). Step 3: Calculate raw Potential Acoustic Gain: PAG = 20 × log10[(D0 × D1) ÷ (D2 × Ds)]. Step 4: Subtract 10 × log10(NOM) for open microphones and the 6 dB Feedback Stability Margin (FSM) from PAG, and verify that NAG is less than the adjusted PAG.

clips.label: Question 177, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. The microphone outputs +54.5 dBu, overloading the mixer preamp input stage. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "The microphone outputs +54.5 dBu,…preamp input stage" uses the wrong value, unit, or relationship for the stated quantities. Decisive rule: Mic Output (dBu) = 72 − 94 + (−54.5) + 2.21 = −74.29 dBu, which needs 74.29 dB of gain to reach 0 dBu line level. Since the preamp has only 60 dB of gain, a more sensitive mic (e.g., −35 dBV/Pa → −54.79 dBu) must be specified. Best answer: The mic outputs -74.3 dBu, requiring more than 60 dB of gain.

clips.label: Question 178
clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: Fixed-microphone feedback-suppression filter procedure. Order the four steps for setting narrow input notch filters to suppress acoustic feedback on a fixed microphone before final room equalization. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Mute all other microphones in the room so only the fixed test microphone is active. Step 2: Slowly raise gain on the test microphone and note the first three frequencies that begin to feed back. Step 3: Build three tight-notch (high-Q) parametric filters at those exact frequencies on that microphone's input channel. Step 4: Reset the gain, equalize the overall sound system, then re-engage the notch filters and verify stable operational level.

clips.text: Exam area C. Topic: EDID negotiation handshake sequence over HPD and DDC. Put the steps of the digital video Extended Display Identification Data (EDID) negotiation process between a source and a display sink in their exact chronological order. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Hot Plug Detection (HPD) 5 V line asserts at startup and the display sink acknowledges the connection. Step 2: The source sends a request for EDID capabilities over the Display Data Channel (DDC). Step 3: The display sink transmits its EDID block (and any extension blocks) back to the source over the DDC. Step 4: The source outputs video and audio matching the nearest approximation to the sink's preferred native resolution, refresh rate, and color space.

clips.label: Question 192

Order the steps for reviewing an updated Architectural & Engineering (A&E) drawing package and revising the conceptual AV design to match site conditions. Arrange these steps from first to last. Step 1: Verify the drawing scale against a known architectural dimension and confirm consistent measurement units across all imported CAD files. Step 2: Cross-check plan views, reflected ceiling plans, elevations, and building sections for structural, HVAC, lighting, sprinkler, and millwork clashes. Step 4: Update the AV drawings, specifications, and allied-trade coordination notes and obtain stakeholder sign-off on the revised design.

clips.label: Question 229, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Deploying mixed panel production batches with high-gain ambient light rejecting optical projection coatings. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "Deploying mixed panel production batches…projection coatings" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. Best answer: Panel color calibration, bezel placement clear of telemetry, and proper viewing sightlines.

Camera autofocus mechanisms cannot acquire focal lock on matte gray surfaces beyond two meters. Option B. Glossy white creates glare and underexposes the presenter's face via camera auto-iris. Option C. Glossy white boards increase high-frequency acoustic reflections that destabilize echo cancellation. Option D. Matte gray markerboards reflect sufficient light to function effectively as front-projection screens.

Option C. NAC grants access based on device identity, compliance posture, and connection method. Option D. NAC converts incoming TCP control streams into analog relay contact closures for lighting.

In an auditorium with a stage monitor and a videowall, audio and video exhibit lip-sync errors. What is the proper fix? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Reduce digital audio sample rates from 48 kHz to 44.1 kHz to advance acoustic waveform timing. Option C. Relocate auditorium loudspeakers fifty feet farther from audience seating to introduce natural acoustic delay. Option D. Add electronic delay to faster signals so all outputs align with the most-delayed display.

clips.text: Option A. Enable HDMI EDID auto-lip-sync on the matrix switcher to calculate multi-display average latency offsets. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "Enable HDMI EDID auto-lip-sync on the…latency offsets" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. clips.label: Question 270
clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Checking rack thermal gradient and opposing fan airflow during integration. A video processor overheats because the unit below exhausts hot air where the processor draws intake air. What is the fix? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Seal all cabinet ventilation slots with aluminum foil tape to contain internal cold air volume. Option B. Reorder equipment layout and install baffle panels to prevent hot exhaust recirculation. Option C. Remove chassis top covers from active processors to vent trapped internal heat into the rack. Option D. Relocate heavy battery backup modules to the uppermost rack positions to improve overall air exhaust.

Enforce verification phases as strict gates; require completion and sign-off before advancing. Option D. Postpone all system verification inspections until the end of the initial one-year warranty period.

clips.label: Question 280, option A rationale
clips.text: Option A. Spot meter in foot-candles for illuminance; incident meter in candelas per square meter for luminance. Incorrect. Not this one: The choice "Spot meter in foot-candles for illuminance;…meter for luminance" addresses a related concern but omits or misorders the decisive requirement in this situation. Decisive rule: Illuminance (incident light arriving at a desk or screen) is measured with an incident meter in lux or foot-candles (1 fc ≈ 10.76 lx); luminance (light reflected/emitted toward the eye) is measured with a spot meter in cd/m² (nits) or foot-lamberts (1 fL ≈ 3.43 cd/m²). Best answer: Incident meter in lux/fc for illuminance; spot meter in cd/m2 or fL for luminance.

clips.text: Exam area D. Topic: Verifying digital audio full-scale headroom (-18 to -20 dBFS nominal). Why is nominal digital audio operating level typically aligned to -18 dBFS or -20 dBFS rather than 0 dBFS? Choose the single best answer. Option A. Digital signal processors achieve optimal warmth and analog harmonics when driven above 0 dBFS. Option B. Calibrating nominal levels to -20 dBFS reduces digital converter resolution from 24 bits to 8 bits. Option C. 0 dBFS is the hard clipping ceiling; alignment preserves 18 to 20 dB of headroom. Option D. Audio converters cannot decode digital bitstreams if peak program signals fall below -12 dBFS.

segments.label: Question
segments.text: Why is Reverberation Time (RT60) valid for large auditoriums but not a valid primary metric for small conference rooms?

segments.label: Response instruction
segments.text: Choose the single best answer.

segments.label: Option A
segments.text: Option A. Acoustic sound waves travel significantly faster across small enclosed volumes than in large concert halls.

segments.label: Option B
segments.text: Option B. Small conference rooms exhibit an invariant RT60 of fifteen seconds across all audible acoustic octave bands.

segments.label: Option C
segments.text: Option C. RT60 assumes a diffuse sound field; small rooms are dominated by early reflections and room modes.

segments.label: Option D
segments.text: Option D. RT60 measures physical partition sound transmission loss rather than internal acoustic sound decay time.

Best answer: RT60 assumes a diffuse sound field; small rooms are dominated by early reflections and room modes.
